findings.explanation: cgroup v2 cpu.stat reports usage_usec, user_usec, system_usec, nr_periods, nr_throttled, throttled_usec, nr_bursts and burst_usec, with all durations in microseconds. throttled_time in nanoseconds and cpuacct.usage are cgroup v1 names. On v2 hosts the throttled-time and usage math has no matching field, or is off by 1000x if throttled_usec is aliased to throttled_time.
findings.quote: scripted reads of cgroup v2 cpu.stat (nr_periods, nr_throttled, throttled_time)
findings.suggested_fix: List the v2 fields (nr_periods, nr_throttled, throttled_usec, usage_usec) separately from the v1 fields (throttled_time in ns, cpuacct.usage in ns), and state that the microsecond fields must be multiplied by 1000 before reuse in nanosecond math.

findings.explanation: Splunk_TA_nix has no cgroup input and no linux:cgroup or procfs:loadavg sourcetype. Its documented sourcetypes are cpu, vmstat, top, ps, df, iostat and similar. The implementation and detailedImplementation lines 'Deploy Splunk_TA_nix linux:cgroup cpu.stat scrapes' and 'procfs:loadavg collection via Splunk_TA_nix modular input' describe inputs that do not exist.
findings.quote: Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux ([Splunkbase 833](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/833)) supplies linux:cgroup and procfs style host telemetry.
findings.suggested_fix: Say that linux:cgroup and procfs:loadavg come from a customer-written scripted input that reads cpu.stat and /proc/loadavg. The alternatives are the OpenTelemetry docker_stats receiver or the Engine API stats cpu_stats.throttling_data. For host load, point to the TA_nix vmstat or cpu sourcetypes.

findings.explanation: The lab container is started with --cpus=0.25. That flag sets HostConfig.NanoCpus (250000000), while CpuQuota and CpuPeriod stay 0, and the daemon derives the CFS quota at runtime. Path B would therefore report 0 0, and responders would chase a 'props gap' that does not exist. The same mistake appears in Step 2: 'values are negative one for unlimited'. Unset CpuQuota is 0 in inspect; -1 only appears in cgroup v1 cfs_quota_us.
findings.quote: docker inspect lab-throttle --format '{{.HostConfig.CpuQuota}} {{.HostConfig.CpuPeriod}}' must match cfs_quota_us and cfs_period_us fields in Splunk after normalization. Mismatches indicate props gaps
findings.suggested_fix: Validate HostConfig.NanoCpus for --cpus containers, and CpuQuota/CpuPeriod only when --cpu-quota/--cpu-period were used. Describe unlimited as CpuQuota=0 and NanoCpus=0 in docker inspect.

findings.explanation: KEP-2625 is the 'SMT aware cpumanager policy' (full-pcpus-only option). It has nothing to do with cgroup v2 CPU quota, so Case B's 'review KEP-2625 era guidance on cgroup v2 cpu quota behavior' points readers at the wrong document. The URL is also only the sig-node directory.
findings.quote: Kubernetes enhancement — KEP-2625 cgroup v2 optional CPU quota
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the KEP-2625 reference and the Case B mention. If burst behaviour matters, cite the kernel CFS bandwidth control document (cpu.max.burst).

findings.explanation: The integration guide defines the indexes container and linux, not metrics_oti, containers or os. The sibling UCs disagree too: UC-3.1.2 uses index=os sourcetype=linux:cgroup and UC-3.1.4 uses index=oti_containers sourcetype=linux:cgroup:memory. Readers cannot tell where cgroup data actually lands.
findings.quote: index=metrics_oti OR index=containers OR index=os sourcetype=linux:cgroup
findings.suggested_fix: Align dataSources, implementation and the sibling UCs on the guide's index names (container / linux) and one cgroup sourcetype naming scheme.

findings.explanation: A five-minute schedule over a window snapped to the previous whole hour rescans the same closed hour twelve times. That produces duplicate alerts, and detection lags by up to two hours for a high-criticality performance UC.
findings.quote: Save container_uc_3_1_3_cpu_throttling every five minutes on earliest=-1h@h latest=@h
findings.suggested_fix: Either run hourly at a few minutes past the hour over -1h@h to @h, or run every five minutes over a rolling window such as -15m to now with alert throttling.

findings.explanation: This is authoring-generator residue (a schema self-check), not guidance for an operator. The same goes for 'Fenced SPL for runbooks must match the spl JSON field byte-for-byte' and the 'six mandated severity strings' wording.
findings.quote: Closing checklist: monitoringType lists Performance and Capacity; splunkPillar Observability; cimModels includes Performance; five step headers use plain text with em dashes; Step 3 fenced SPL matches the spl field exactly
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the closing checklist and the generator-contract sentences, and keep only the operational steps.

findings.explanation: The hostmetrics receiver does not read per-container cpu.stat throttling counters. Per-container throttling comes from the docker_stats receiver (container.cpu.throttling_data.* metrics), and its field names do not match the SPL coalesce list.
findings.quote: Splunk OpenTelemetry Collector for Linux ... can scrape cgroup CPU counters
findings.suggested_fix: Name the receiver explicitly (docker_stats receiver throttling_data metrics) and give the props or field aliases that map it to nr_periods, nr_throttled and throttled time.

findings.explanation: Neither source appears in references. Buffer's widely cited CPU-limits post is believed to date from 2019, not 2017, and no specific Cloudflare NGINX container-throttling post is identified.
findings.quote: Buffer's 2017 Kubernetes CPU throttling incident narrative, and Cloudflare engineering posts on NGINX container CPU throttling failures
findings.suggested_fix: Check the publication year and URL of the Buffer post and whether the Cloudflare post exists. Then add both as references with URLs, or remove them.

findings.explanation: The Brendan Gregg reference points at the blog index rather than a specific CFS or throttling article, and the Lantern reference is about Docker logs, not CPU metrics.
findings.suggested_fix: Link the specific article that is relied on, and drop the logging-focused Lantern page or replace it with a metrics-relevant one.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified by a generic repository handle, yet it contains a non-existent TA sourcetype, wrong cgroup v2 field names and SPL that cannot return rows. No SME sign-off is evident.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade status until an SME has validated the data source and run the search on a real cgroup v2 host.

findings.explanation: Nothing in the UC maps to Application_State, and that model may be deprecated in current CIM releases. Host CPU load in Performance is only a loose proxy for per-container throttling.
findings.suggested_fix: Check whether Application_State is still in the current CIM release, and remove it (and its mention in dataModelAcceleration) if it is not used.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: With `streamstats window=2 current=t`, last(nr_periods), last(nr_throttled), last(throttled_time_ns), last(cpu_usage_ns) and last(_time) all return the current event's own values, because the current event is the last one seen in the window. So periods_delta=0 and sec_delta=0 on every row, and `where periods_delta>0 AND ... sec_delta>0` drops everything. The search never alerts. Use `current=f window=1 last(...)` (or window=2 current=t with first()) to get the previous sample.

The SPL only coalesces the v1 throttled_time (ns) and cpuacct_usage names. cgroup v2 throttled_usec and usage_usec are never read, so throttled_wall_pct and quota_pct_used are null on v2 hosts, and they would be 1000x low if the fields were aliased without converting units.

cpuset_span replaces '-' with ',' and counts the elements, so a range such as '0-63' counts as 2 CPUs. Broad cpusets are flagged cpuset_narrow=1, which raises high_cpuset_numa_misplacement falsely. Ranges must be expanded (end-start+1) before counting.

There is a severity ladder gap. A sample with throttle_pct>=90 whose 5-sample average (throttle_pct_sustained) is below 90 matches neither the critical branch nor 'high_throttled_70_to_90pct' (throttle_pct<90), so the worst point-in-time throttling returns no row. The medium branch's `throttle_peak_1h>=30` test is always true when throttle_pct>=30, so the 'chronic' qualifier is not enforced.

The cfs_cpus fallback treats CpuQuota=0 and NanoCpus=0 as no limit, which is correct. But the docker:inspect subsearch defaults a missing CpuQuota to -1 and a missing CpuPeriod to 100000, so a missing inspect record cannot be told apart from an unlimited container. container_name is not present in raw cgroup cpu.stat reads either, so the container_owner join on host_id/container_name usually misses unless the collector enriches it.

CIM Performance fields are rooted at All_Performance: the CPU dataset is All_Performance.CPU and the field is All_Performance.cpu_load_percent. `Performance.cpu_load_percent` with `nodename=Performance.CPU` returns nothing. Host CPU load is also not a container throttling signal.

summary: The CFS throttling idea is sound and the risk briefing and grandma text are good. But the UC gives the wrong cgroup v2 cpu.stat field names and units, credits a linux:cgroup sourcetype and a loadavg modular input to Splunk_TA_nix (it has neither), and tells readers to validate docker inspect CpuQuota after --cpus (it reads 0). The SPL's streamstats delta logic cannot produce any rows.
